Revised assessment incorporating economic literature:
- The FOMC’s pledge to keep the funds rate at 0–0.25% and continue sizable Treasury/MBS purchases until “substantial further progress” is consistent with modern interest-rate targeting and corridor/floor systems (interest on reserves and ON RRP as bounds), as documented in central bank operating frameworks where short-term policy rates are the primary instrument and the corridor anchors money market rates.
- The commitment to let inflation run “moderately above 2%” to average 2% over time reflects inflation-forecast targeting and average-inflation targeting principles (Svensson; Clarida and co-authors), which aim to anchor expectations and mitigate the classic inflation bias under discretion (Barro-Gordon) while recognizing the risks of real-time mismeasurement of gaps (Orphanides).
- Asset purchases support accommodative financial conditions by affecting term premia and the yield curve (Rudebusch; Piazzesi), complementing the near-zero policy rate when the ZLB binds and simple Taylor rules would otherwise prescribe insufficient accommodation.
- Despite these supportive measures, the statement emphasizes pandemic-related downside risks to activity and employment; literature on risk-management monetary policy supports maintaining an accommodative stance under such uncertainty.

Net tone: cautious but policy-supportive. Relative to a purely risk-focused excerpt, the broader framework and commitment temper the negativity.
